TWO PASSAGES FROM AZRIELI FOUNDATION HOLOCAUST SURVIVOR MEMOIRS THAT NAME CAMP KANAWANA.

Both books are lending-restricted on the Internet Archive and CANNOT be read from here. Each
passage below was assembled from overlapping phrase queries against Open Library's search-inside
endpoint on 2026-09-06, joining windows of about a dozen words. THESE ARE RECONSTRUCTIONS, not
transcriptions, and nothing outside the quoted stretch has been read.

================================================================================
1. Judy Abrams, "Retenue par un fil / Une question de chance"
   (French edition of "Tenuous Threads", Azrieli Foundation, 2013)
   Internet Archive item retenueparunfil0000unse, scan leaf 254.

QUERIES: "Camp Kanawana" ; "rejoint le camp Kanawana du YMCA" ;
         "Il m'a écrit de longues lettres décrivant" ; "appelé Escobar, il a pour sa part" ;
         "dans un camp de vacances privé, appelé Escobar" ; "lée ses voyages"

RECONSTRUCTED:

  ... aimait pas moins. Durant l'été, lorsque je suis partie dans un camp de vacances privé,
  appelé Escobar, il a pour sa part rejoint le camp Kanawana du YMCA. Il m'a écrit de longues
  lettres décrivant de manière détail[-]lée ses voyages en canoë dans la nature sauvage des
  Laurentides ...

DATING, from the author and not from the passage: Judy Abrams was born in Budapest on
28 April 1937 and came to Montreal in 1949. A summer of her Montreal adolescence puts this in
the early or mid 1950s.

WHAT IS NOT IN THE RECOVERED TEXT: who "il" is. He is not named and the relationship is not
stated in any window recovered. No year is given. Do not infer either.

================================================================================
2. Michael Kutz, "If, By Miracle" (Azrieli Foundation, 2013)
   Internet Archive item ifbymiracle0000kutz, scan leaf 190.
   The book's own index carries "Camp Kanawana, 87", so the printed page is 87.

QUERIES: "Camp Kanawana" ; "diabetic children from Camp Kanawana" ;
         "as well as for diabetic children" ; "bedridden or in wheelchairs, as well as" ;
         "we arranged a party for the children" ; "refreshments and singing songs with them" ;
         "Hospital, bringing them toys and refreshments" ;
         "Our organization's donations helped create" ;
         "one of the largest science libraries at the hospital" ;
         "Through the Knights of Pythias"

RECONSTRUCTED:

  ... [we visited the children] at the Montreal Children's Hospital, bringing them toys and
  refreshments and singing songs with them. Every December, we arranged a party for the
  children, most of whom were bedridden or in wheelchairs, as well as for diabetic children
  from Camp Kanawana. Our organization's donations helped create one of the largest science
  libraries at the hospital. Through the Knights of Pythias, I also visited hundreds of war
  veterans ...

The bracketed opening is supplied: the window begins mid-sentence at "Hospital", and the words
before it were not recovered, so the subject and verb are inferred from the sentence that
follows. "Our organization" is the Knights of Pythias, named two sentences later.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the years; whether the diabetic children came to Kanawana as a session
or as individuals; and whether the December party was held at the hospital or at camp. Kutz was
born in 1930 and settled in Canada after the war, so the period is his adult life in Montreal.
